title: KASA to Establish the Foundation for Korea Positioning System Utilization in Collaboration with Industry
text:
– KASA Hosts the 7th SOS Consultative Meeting with Companies in the Satellite Navigation Application Sector
– Discussion on Establishing a KPS Utilization Base and Fostering Growth in KPS-related Industries
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held the 7th SOS (Speedy On-site Solution) Consultative Meeting with companies in the satellite navigation application sector on June 25 (Thursday) at the LIG D&A Daejeon House.
The meeting was organized to identify industry demand from the development stage of the Korea Positioning System (KPS) and to establish policies for activating KPS utilization by discovering support measures required in the industrial field.
KPS is a satellite navigation system that Korea is independently developing to provide ultra-precise positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) information for Korea and its surrounding regions without relying on the U.S. Global Positioning System (GPS). It is expected to be utilized in various industrial sectors, including navigation for automobiles and ships, emergency rescue, and disaster prediction.
A total of 12 companies* in the fields of satellite navigation receiver development and location-based application services attended the meeting. KASA shared the current status of KPS development and future utilization plans, and directly collected feedback from industry stakeholders.
* Dusitech, MicroInfinity, MBC, Samsung Electronics, Samyoung PNT, Synerex, Insung International, InterGravity, Hyundai Motor Company, KT, LG Uplus, LIG D&A
The companies emphasized the need to expand applications across various industries and commercialize services based on KPS. In particular, they stated in unison that it is essential to establish a foundation for the utilization of satellite navigation services through the disclosure of KPS signal design and service data, as well as the creation of a supportive utilization environment.
In addition, they proposed that, in order to expand the utilization of KPS, it is necessary to take measures such as phased disclosure of signal and service information, establishment of testing environments and certification and verification infrastructure, support for the development of satellite navigation-based application services, linkage with Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites and space services, and establishment of a foundation for the commercialization of high-precision positioning services.
Administrator Taeseog Oh of KASA stated, “KPS is a core infrastructure that will support the competitiveness of future innovative industries and the stability of national services, and it is important to actively reflect industry demand from the development stage,” adding, “We will actively incorporate the insights discussed in this meeting into policies and support measures for expanding KPS utilization and fostering the satellite navigation industry, and we plan to build a KPS utilization ecosystem through continuous communication with industry.”

title: KASA Advances AI-Powered Space Exploration Mobility beyond Remote Control and into Autonomous Navigation
text:
– Industry-Academia-Research Expert Meeting Held to Improve Efficiency of 2032 Lunar Exploration Rover Mission
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held an expert meeting on the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in space exploration robotics on June 24 (Wed) at the Paradise Hotel in Busan, and discussed the introduction of AI into space exploration mobility systems.
The meeting was organized to enhance the operational efficiency of the lunar rover to be deployed in Korea’s upcoming 2032 lunar landing mission. The lunar rover is designed to traverse the lunar surface and support various scientific and technological payloads during the lunar daytime period (up to 14 Earth days).
In particular, to maximize mission efficiency, technologies are required for optimal path planning, such as minimizing energy consumption during traversal within a limited operational timeframe and avoiding hazards during mobility. By integrating rapidly advancing AI technologies, the rover will be able to make autonomous decisions and carry out mobility tasks, significantly improving mission efficiency.
The meeting also covered Korea’s lunar exploration roadmap, international cases of AI applications in space exploration robotics, and differentiation strategies for AI-based mobility technologies in the domestic industry. Experts from industry, academia, and research institutions (Korea Automotive Technology Institute, Unmanned Exploration Lab, Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, etc.) participated in discussions on the application of AI in the 2032 lunar surface exploration mission, as well as the potential use of AI and robotics in future lunar bases.
In addition, discussions on advanced rover capability enhancement included autonomous identification of scientific targets by the rover, terrain recognition technologies to detect and classify hazards such as rocks using machine-learning-based image analysis, and route optimization, which includes autonomous navigation map generation calculating terrain slope and elevation data.
Administrator Taeseog Oh of KASA stated, “We will actively support the convergence of Korea’s strengths in robotics and AI technologies so that new industries in space exploration can be created, enabling deep space exploration extending from the Moon to Mars and beyond.”

title: Government and Industry to Jointly Launch AI and Satellite Data Convergence Services
text:
– Kick-off Meeting for “AI-based Satellite Data Utilization Service Expansion Project” held on June 22
– Demonstration Projects planned in Jeju and Jeollanam-do in 2026 to Analyze Geohazard Zones and Manage Marine Environment Using Satellite Imagery
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held a kick-off meeting for the 2026 new “AI-based Satellite Data Utilization Service Expansion Project,” at the National Information Society Agency (NIA) on June 22 at 14:00 KST, and announced the full-scale provision of AI-satellite data convergence services in collaboration with companies and local governments. These services refer to subscription-based models that apply AI-based analysis of satellite imagery through cloud infrastructure to support local administrative tasks such as urban management, marine monitoring, and disaster response.
The project was designed based on industry feedback collected through a 2025 KASA-hosted meeting with 23 satellite utilization companies in 2025. It also reflects the results of a 2025 demand survey on satellite data utilization pilot services for local governments, which identified 13 service model tasks across 9 municipalities. The initiative aims to validate companies’ AI-satellite data convergence services in cooperation with local governments, thereby securing 13 industrial performance cases that will serve as a foundation for overseas expansion by 2030.
For the 2026 program, two demonstration projects were selected through a public call (April 2-May 7, 2026):
➊ Geohazard Zone Analysis Based on Satellite Imagery
This project aims to identify and analyze high-risk ground deformation areas in Jeju Island using AI-based satellite image analysis. The lead implementing organization (service model supplier) is Soda System, with Innopam as a participating organization (supporter of service model demonstration), along with Jeju Special Self-Governing Province.
➋ Smart Marine Environmental Management System
This project aims to build and operate a smart system for monitoring and managing marine debris using satellite data. The lead implementing organization is UST21, with participation from MuhanIT, 3DLabs, Our Sea of East Asia Network, and Sinan County, Jeollanam-do.
Through this initiative, KASA aims to foster a new industry integrating AI and satellite data to address regional challenges, strengthen the foundation of the space industry, and establish key drivers enabling Korean companies to expand into global markets. The Administration also plans to strengthen collaboration with NIA to ensure that cloud-based satellite data services translate into tangible industrial competitiveness.
Administrator Taeseog Oh stated, “Through this project, we will provide citizen-centered AI-satellite data convergence services to local governments and actively support Korean companies so that their 13 service models can enter the global market by 2030.”

title: KASA Continues On-site Industry Engagement through 2nd Aerospace Industry Development Council Meeting
text:
– 28 Companies from Aviation Manufacturing, Satellites, Launch Vehicles, and Future Technologies Participate
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held the 2nd meeting of the Public-Private Council for Aerospace Industry Development on June 22 (Mon) at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul to continue in-depth discussions with private companies aimed at fostering a private-sector-led aerospace industry.
This second meeting was attended by 28 companies across four divisions (aviation manufacturing, satellite development and utilization of satellite data, launch vehicles, and future technologies) that had participated in the first meeting held in February, along with KASA Administrator Taeseog Oh and Jouhahn Lee, Secretary to the President for Science, Technology and Research. Participants engaged in open and candid discussions on the development of the aerospace industry.
Prior to discussing the main agenda, KASA shared updates with participating companies on the status of follow-up actions and implementation progress regarding key suggestions raised during the first meeting. The Administration has categorized the proposals into 16 tasks and is prioritizing implementation of urgent issues. In particular, a KRW 200 billion New Space Fund for corporate growth support, a sector that has seen strong industry demand, is scheduled to begin investment in September.
Participants also reviewed trends in the aerospace industry and exchanged views on future development strategies in a free and open manner. In-depth discussions were held on various measures to promote the aerospace industry, including ways to stimulate public-sector demand in the space sector and improvements to legal and institutional frameworks. KASA plans to incorporate industry feedback into future policy direction.
Jouhahn Lee, Science, Technology and Research Secretary at the Presidential Office, emphasized that “the aerospace industry is a core future growth engine directly linked to national competitiveness,” adding that “the Presidential Office will actively cooperate with KASA to ensure that the voices from the industrial field are rapidly translated into tangible policies and budgets,” thereby underscoring the government’s strong commitment to fostering the aerospace industry.
Administrator Taeseog Oh stated, “Just as we carefully reflected the valuable feedback received in the first meeting, we will faithfully incorporate today’s opinions into our policy formulation and implementation process,” adding, “KASA will continue to make efforts to consolidate whole-of-government capabilities and provide practical support measures that industry can directly feel, so that the aerospace industry can develop into a key national strategic industry.”

title: Supporting Space Equipment Development by Companies and Universities through Reducing the Burden of Space Environment Testing
text:
– KASA Announces the “2026 Space Environment Testing Support Program”
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced that it will recruit eligible organizations for the “2026 Space Environment Testing Support Program” from June 22 (Mon) to July 6 (Mon), in order to enhance the quality and export competitiveness of space equipment developed by domestic companies and universities.
The Space Environment Testing Support Program provides financial support for costs incurred in conducting tests under simulated space conditions—such as thermal, vacuum, and radiation environments—to improve the reliability of space equipment developed by domestic small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), mid-sized companies, and universities. The scope of testing includes not only orbital environments expected to be encountered during space missions by space equipment and components, but also ground test and launch environments.
Detailed program announcements and application procedures for the “2026 Space Environment Testing Support Program” are available on the KASA website (www.kasa.go.kr) or the Korea Association for Space Technology Promotion website (www.kasp.or.kr).
Any domestic SME, mid-sized company, or university developing in-house space equipment is eligible to apply. Selection will be made through document screening and in-person evaluation based on a comprehensive assessment of suitability of the proposed items, appropriateness of the project budget, suitability of the testing institution, and expected economic and technical impact.
For selected companies, up to 75% of testing costs will be supported, with a maximum of KRW 60 million per year, while universities will receive 100% support up to KRW 30 million per year. This represents a 50% increase in the support ceiling compared to the previous year, enabling selected organizations to conduct a wider range of space environment tests.
* Corporate co-payment rates: 25% for SMEs, 40% for mid-sized companies
Since space equipment is difficult to repair or maintain after launch, pre-verification through ground-based space environment testing is essential. However, the high cost of such testing places a financial burden on companies and universities. This program therefore helps alleviate the cost burden of private-sector space development and contributes to strengthening product competitiveness.
In the previous year, 11 companies and 1 university were selected, achieving notable outcomes including one export case and eight domestic procurement deliveries. In addition, support for universities developing space systems such as CubeSats has contributed to strengthening university capabilities in space systems development and fostering future specialists. 
* 12 organizations selected in 2025: STEPLab, APSI, Gigalane, LUMIR, Satrec Initiative, Edelway, Ace Technologies, Genohco, Genew, HANCOM InSpace, Korea Aerospace Industries, Chosun University
Administrator Oh stated, “The Space Environment Testing Support Program is essential for enhancing the technological capabilities of industry and academia and accelerating product innovation,” adding, “We will continue to expand testing infrastructure and support programs to create an environment in which domestic companies and universities can develop innovative and challenging space technologies.”

title: Announcement of Public Call for Candidate Sites to host the Second Space Center
text:
– Nationwide Local Governments Invited to Participate
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced that it will conduct a public call for candidate sites for the construction of the Second Space Center from June 22 (Mon) to August 6 (Thu), targeting local governments nationwide.
KASA is preparing to establish the Second Space Center in order to strengthen the foundation of the national space industry by securing infrastructure capable of stably responding to the operation of reusable launch vehicles and demand for frequent satellite launches, thereby concentrating capabilities in research and development, manufacturing, and testing and evaluation.
Major space powers such as the United States (Kennedy Space Center, Vandenberg Space Force Base, etc.) and Europe (Guiana Space Centre, Andøya Spaceport, etc.) operate multiple launch sites to ensure launch flexibility and industrial competitiveness. Meanwhile, Korea currently relies on a single launch site, the Naro Space Center, which limits its ability to diversify space transportation capabilities, including support for private small-scale and solid-fuel launches.
The Second Space Center is expected to include facilities necessary for reusable launch operations, such as reusable launch vehicle launch pads and landing facilities. In the future, it will support frequent launch operations of next-generation reusable launch vehicles and various commercial launch vehicles, thereby enabling national space missions such as Earth observation, communications, and navigation satellite launches, as well as lunar and Mars exploration.
Local governments wishing to host the Second Space Center may refer to the official announcement posted on the KASA website (www.kasa.go.kr) for detailed information.
Submitted proposals will be reviewed by a selection committee, and the final results are scheduled to be announced in October.
Administrator Taeseog Oh stated, “The Second Space Center is a key infrastructure for a qualitative leap forward in the Korean space industry,” adding, “Based on active participation and cooperation from local governments, we will create a new launch hub where the space industry can grow to its full potential.”

title: KASA Secures Key Space Technologies including Fiber-Optic Gyroscopes and Launch Vehicle Coating Technologies
text:
– Eight Space New Technologies have been Confirmed to Support the Industrialization of Domestic Space Technology
The Korea Aerospace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held a ceremony at 2:00 p.m. on June 17 at its headquarters in Sacheon to announce the “Second Space New Technologies” and award designation certificates.
The Space New Technology Designation Program is a system that identifies technologies that have been either developed for the first time in Korea or improved from foreign technologies, and that demonstrate outstanding novelty, advancement, and high potential for value creation. This is the second implementation of the program, following its launch last year. 
* First Space New Technology designation status: 52 applications received, 5 technologies designated. Certificates were issued in January 2026.
A total of 30 technologies were submitted for this round of selection, including 19 in the satellite sector, 5 in the launch vehicle sector, and 6 in space observation, exploration, and other fields. KASA established field-specific review committees and conducted a rigorous three-stage evaluation process—document review, on-site inspection, and comprehensive assessment—based on innovation, marketability, and public value.
The final selected Space New Technologies feature high technology readiness level and successful localization, with four technologies selected each in the satellite and launch vehicle sectors, totaling eight designated technologies. These technologies are considered essential for the advancement of the domestic space industry and are expected to generate significant economic ripple effects.
In the satellite sector, the selected four items primarily focus on localization of core components. The “Fiber-Optic Gyroscope for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites” by FiberPro detects rotation using optical fibers to enable long-term precise attitude control of satellites, and is expected to be widely applied across various satellite platforms through domestic localization of key components. The “GNSS Receiver for Geostationary Satellites” by DusiTech stably tracks weak signals from long distances to precisely determine satellite position and timing. By using components not subject to export restrictions, it enables independent satellite development and operation. The “10 mN-class Hall Thruster and Hollow Cathode for Small LEO Satellites” by Cosmo Bee is a high-efficiency electric propulsion technology that enhances applicability in future satellite markets, including Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) and deep-space exploration, through localization of key components. The “Space-grade, high-reliability SRAM (Static Random Access Memory)” by MID is a semiconductor technology that securely stores and processes satellite data in extreme environments, securing domestic supply capability for space-grade memory previously dependent on imports.
In the launch vehicle sector, selected four technologies include those enhancing engine performance and achieving manufacturing independence. The “Anti-oxidation Coating Technology for Liquid Rocket Engine Metals” by Vitzro Nextech prevents ignition of internal components under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions, increasing applicability in reusable launch vehicles through localized coating materials and processes. The “High-pressure and Cryogenic Inter-Stage Umbilical Technology for Space Launch Vehicle” by Hanyang ENG enables safe fuel transfer of cryogenic propellants and secure separation during liftoff, achieving technological independence through in-house testing facilities. title: Aircraft Engine Competitiveness Begins with Materials
text:
- KASA Launches Materials and Components Development Program
- KRW 42.9 Billion Investment Over 5 Years to Develop 5 Key Materials and 4 Core Components
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held the kickoff meeting for the “Development of High-Strength Materials and Components for Aircraft Gas Turbine Engine Structures” project from June 16 to 17 at KB Ingenium in Sacheon, officially launching the research and development initiative.
The project aims to invest a total of KRW 42.9 billion (KRW 29.7 billion in government funding) over the next five years to develop five types of lightweight and heat-resistant materials and four key components. Beyond simple localization of aircraft engine materials and parts, the initiative is strategically designed to secure full-cycle technological capabilities—from material design and manufacturing to testing, data accumulation, and product application—thereby enhancing the added value of Korea’s aviation industry.
Led by an aircraft engine system developer, 9 materials companies and 11 universities and research institutes will carry out R&D in three areas: lightweight castings and forgings, high-strength materials, and ultra-heat-resistant materials and precision casting technologies.
At the kickoff meeting, the lead organization presented detailed research objectives and implementation plans, followed by presentations on the roles of participating research institutions and specific collaboration strategies.
A total of 20 R&D companies and institutions participating in three sub-projects presented their research objectives and implementation plans, and reviewed technology development directions and cooperation frameworks through expert consultation. The session also covered guidelines for national R&D program implementation and the research funding management system, sharing measures to strengthen project execution capabilities and establish a research management framework.
Participants agreed to achieve technological self-reliance in key aircraft engine materials and components, foster close cooperation, and maintain regular technical exchanges in order to maximize project outcomes.
Aircraft engines are core systems that determine both the performance and safety of aircraft. The materials used in these engines must maintain stability under extreme high-temperature and high-pressure conditions while meeting stringent certification standards.
In particular, aircraft engine materials represent a highly advanced field that requires long-term technological accumulation rather than simple manufacturing capability. Only a small number of countries, including the United States (GE, Pratt & Whitney), the United Kingdom (Rolls-Royce), and France (Safran), possess fully integrated technological capabilities in this field, making it a highly entry-restricted sector.
Historically, Korea’s reliance on imported engines has limited opportunities to accumulate materials and components technologies. Individual companies face significant barriers due to long development cycles, high certification costs, and the dominance of established global players, resulting in a structurally high entry barrier.
As a result, a vicious cycle of technological dependency and high-cost component imports has persisted. Accordingly, the localization of aircraft engine materials is not merely a matter of supply stability but a strategic task to enhance the technological capability and industrial competitiveness of Korea’s aviation ecosystem.
KASA plans to incorporate expert feedback from the kickoff meeting to refine the research direction and operate systematic project management through quarterly and semi-annual technical exchange meetings and milestone review sessions. In addition, the agency intends to expand R&D in aviation materials and components, gradually building a foundation for independent aircraft engine development and strengthening the technological competitiveness of Korea’s aviation industry.
Administrator Taeseog Oh emphasized, “Aircraft engines are a core field that determines the competitiveness of a nation’s aviation industry, and the materials and components technologies that support them are the starting point for independent engine development and industrial value creation.”

title: KASA to Host 7th CubeSat Competition
text:
– Full Support from Satellite Development to Launch and Mission Operations
– Application Period: June 17 – July 10
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced the launch of the “7th CubeSat Competition” to foster outstanding talent in the space sector and expand the foundation of satellite development among university and graduate students. Applications will be accepted from June 17 to July 10, 2026.
Since its inception in 2012, the CubeSat Competition has served as a flagship satellite development program in Korea, enabling participants to directly plan, design, and execute satellite missions, thereby deepening their understanding of the full space development lifecycle and fostering innovative ideas for space utilization.
For this year’s competition, a total of seven teams will be selected: five teams in the beginner category and two teams in the advanced category. The selected teams will complete satellite development by 2028, with launch planned using domestic launch vehicles, including the Korea Space Launch Vehicle II (Nuri) or domestic private-sector launch vehicles.
Of the six satellites developed in the 6th competition, four were successfully launched aboard the fourth flight of the Nuri rocket in November 2025 and are currently operating their missions. The remaining two satellites are scheduled to be launched on the fifth Nuri flight in the second half of 2026.
* Nuri Flight 4: Seoul National University (SNGULITE), Inha University (INHA RoSAT), KAIST (K-HERO), Sejong University (SPIRONE). Nuri Flight 5: KAIST (GBSAT), Chosun University (CPSat).
The competition will be conducted in two rounds. In the first round, teams will be selected based on presentations of mission concepts and conceptual designs, resulting in 14 finalist teams. In the second round, final selections will be made based on preliminary design evaluations, resulting in seven selected teams.
Selected teams will receive structured training programs, and full financial support will be provided for satellite design and manufacturing costs.
In addition, a workshop will be held on June 24 during the Space Conference of the Korean Society for Aeronautical and Space Sciences, targeting prospective applicants and students nationwide. The workshop will introduce CubeSat development stages and provide practical guidance and participation know-how.
This competition is designed to provide future space professionals with hands-on experience in real-world space development and to help them explore career paths in the space sector through creative mission design. It is also expected to contribute to expanding Korea’s satellite development ecosystem and promoting space culture.
Previous participants of the program have entered the space industry through startups and employment in related organizations, demonstrating tangible outcomes as a human resource development initiative.
Notably, Jae-pil Park, CEO of Nara Space Technology, participated in the first competition in 2012 while at Yonsei University. Based on his experience in satellite development and demonstration of the CANYVAL satellite, he founded a CubeSat development company in 2015, which was listed on KOSDAQ in December 2025.
Administrator Taeseog Oh of KASA stated, “CubeSats are one of the most effective educational platforms for students to experience the full space development process firsthand.” He added, “We hope it will serve as a stepping stone for future space professionals to realize their aspirations and strengthen their capabilities to lead the space industry.”

title: Launch of the Inaugural Future Space Policy Forum
text:
– Gathering Diverse Expert Opinions and Strengthening Recommendations on Increasingly Complex Policy Agendas
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Tae-seog Oh) hosted the inaugural “Future Space Policy Forum” at the Koreana Hotel in Seoul on Monday, June 15, gathering experts to engage in professional discussions on pressing space development agendas.
Amid a rapidly evolving global space landscape, the Future Space Policy Forum is designed to gather in-depth feedback from industry, academic, and research experts on key space development challenges and translate these insights into actionable policy frameworks. The forum functions as a hybrid platform, blending strategic networking in the space sector with the analytical capabilities of a think-tank. KASA oversees the overall management of the forum, with the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) serving as the executive operating body. Furthermore, the forum will concurrently serve as a policy subcommittee under the Space Development Promotion Working Committee, operating under the National Space Council, which governs national space policy. In this role, the forum will actively identify on-site issues to be developed into official policy agendas.
This inaugural meeting, which also marked the official launch of the forum, brought together officials from KASA, KARI, and forum committee members to introduce future operational strategies. This was followed by a keynote presentation on strategic directions amidst the escalating global space race. With global competition intensifying as an extension of the hegemonic rivalry between major powers like the United States and China, participants engaged in a rigorous discussion on the future direction of national policies required to foster South Korea’s domestic space industry and secure space sovereignty.
Subsequent presentations addressed pressing space development challenges, including measures to revitalize procurement and sourcing in the space sector, alongside improvements to key legal frameworks such as the Act on Compensation for Damage Caused by Space Objects. Participants actively exchanged views on strategic approaches to institutionalize these proposals into formal public policy.
Tae-seog Oh, Administrator of KASA, stated, “As space development challenges become increasingly complex and environmental shifts accelerate, the public sector can no longer unilaterally guide policy in the right direction.” He added, “Leveraging the professional recommendations from experts across various fields, I look forward to broadening the horizon of our space development policies and establishing measures that can be tangibly felt on the ground, particularly within the commercial space sector which is now in its nascent stage.”

title: KASA Publishes a Directory of Aircraft Component Testing Infrastructure
text:
– KASA Publishes and Distributes Its First-Ever “Directory of Environmental Testing and Evaluation for Aircraft Components”
– Consolidating Information from Major Testing Institutions Nationwide: Korea’s First Comprehensive Guide to Aircraft Component Testing
– Slashing Information Search Times and Costs: Expected to Accelerate Component Self-Reliance for SMEs
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced on Friday, May 29, the publication and distribution of the “Directory of Environmental Testing and Evaluation for Aircraft Components.” This initiative aims to enhance accessibility to environmental testing for aircraft component manufacturers and promote the utilization of domestic testing infrastructure.
This directory is South Korea’s first comprehensive guide that systematically organizes aircraft component environmental testing and evaluation information, which had previously been scattered across various organizations. Developed from a user-centric perspective, it is designed to help component manufacturers swiftly identify and connect with the appropriate testing and evaluation institutions.
While the domestic aviation industry increasingly recognizes the need for supply chain stabilization and component self-reliance, the scattered nature of testing and evaluation infrastructure across multiple institutions has cost companies significant time and expense in locating suitable facilities.
To resolve these practical bottlenecks on the ground, KASA initiated an internal study in April 2025 and officially commenced the planning of this directory in June of the same year.
To maximize the practical utility of the directory, KASA formed a dedicated task force (TF) to systematically refine the data. The TF integrated a total of 15 institutions, including major organizations such as: KTR (Korea Testing & Research Institute), KTC (Korea Testing Certification Institute), KCL (Korea Conformity Laboratories), KITECH (Korea Institute of Industrial Technology), KTL (Korea Testing Laboratory).
Furthermore, in November 2025, KASA hosted an industry hearing attended by aircraft component manufacturers (the end-users) and experts from testing and evaluation institutions to gather on-site feedback and incorporate necessary improvements, thereby ensuring high practical relevance.
The directory includes the following: Current status of domestic aircraft component testing and evaluation institutions, Major testing infrastructure categorized by environmental testing types, Applicable testing and evaluation fields along with equipment specialized by each institution. Through this directory, KASA expects to alleviate the burden of information searches for enterprises, boost the utilization of testing and evaluation facilities, and streamline the overall process of aircraft component development and validation.
KASA plans to make the directory publicly available on its official website starting May 29, 2026, alongside promotional campaigns. Moving forward, the administration will periodically monitor on-site usage to update and refine the publication.
KASA Administrator Taeseog Oh stated, “This directory holds immense significance as it is the very first initiative to consolidate fragmented aircraft component environmental testing information from a user-centric perspective.” He added, “We will continuously support aircraft component companies so they can utilize necessary infrastructure with greater ease, thereby contributing to component self-reliance and the enhancement of our industry's competitiveness.”

title: KASA Hosts Commemorative Ceremony for the 2nd Aerospace Day
text:
– The 2nd Aerospace Day ceremony was held on May 27 at the KASA headquarters in Sacheon
– Seven government awards were conferred upon meritorious individuals for their outstanding contributions to the aerospace sector
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced that it successfully held the commemorative ceremony for the “2nd Aerospace Day” on Wednesday, May 27, at its headquarters in Sacheon.
“Aerospace Day” is a national commemorative day designated to honor the establishment of KASA on May 27, 2024. Marking its second anniversary this year, the ceremony was organized to celebrate the 2nd anniversary of KASA's opening, reverently recognize the dedication of meritorious individuals who spearheaded the development of the aerospace industry over the past year, and expand public interest and engagement in aerospace.
Held under the slogan “Our Technology, Our Space, a New Era for K-Space,” the event was attended by around 100 key figures and stakeholders from the government, the National Assembly, and industry-academia-research institutes. During the ceremony, official government awards were presented to outstanding contributors to national aerospace advancement.
A total of seven government awards were conferred, including one Order of Science and Technology Merit, one Science and Technology Merit Medal, two Presidential Citation, and three Prime Minister’s Citation.
The Order of Science and Technology Merit was awarded to Hyunsuk Seo, Director of the Satellite Research Department at Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI). He was recognized for his pivotal role in localizing satellite technologies through leading contributions to major domestic satellite programs, including KOMPSAT (Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite), CAS-500 (Compact Advanced Satellite 500), and KPS-1 (Korean Positioning System Satellite).
The Science and Technology Merit Medal went to Hwannil Huh, Professor at Chungnam National University. Professor Huh served as the Vice President of the Korean Society for Aeronautical and Space Sciences and Director of the Korean Society of Propulsion Engineers, and greatly contributed to fostering an aerospace culture by operating the regional rocket launch experience club and rocket educational program.
The Presidential Citation was awarded to two recipients: Eun-hyuk Kim, Principal Researcher at the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI), who laid the groundwork for lunar exploration through the development and operation of payloads for South Korea’s first lunar orbiter, Danuri; and Seung-young Lee, CTO at LIG D&A, who contributed to the development of advanced weapon systems, including the mass production of high-performance observation equipment for fighter jets and the localization of avionics systems.
The Prime Minister’s Citation was awarded to three recipients: Woo Chul Jang, Principal Researcher at Hyundai Wia, for his contribution to localizing landing gears for major aircraft such as the KF-16, T-50, and Surion; Jung Hyun Jo, Principal Researcher at the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI), for establishing a foundation for deep-space exploration through research on satellite orbits; and Chan-Gyeong Im, Principal Researcher at KARI, who oversaw ground facility operations for the 4th Nuri launch and facilitated successful technology transfers.
Furthermore, a variety of cultural programs were held concurrently in the afternoon to offer citizens an accessible and engaging encounter with aerospace science.
Hands-on and educational booths featuring lunar rover simulations, rocket model assembling and launching, and model airplane building were operated around the KASA premises. Additionally, Dr. Yeon-Seok Chae, a former president of KARI, hosted an insightful aerospace talk titled "Reading the Universe."
KASA Administrator Taeseog Oh stated, “I extend my deepest respect and gratitude to all professionals who are sweating night and day across industrial fields nationwide.” He added, “In alignment with the New Space era, where the private sector drives space development, KASA will provide unsparing support to ensure that researchers can fully immerse themselves in innovative research and bold challenges.”

title: KASA Commences Development of Korea’s First Dual-Use Aviation Turbofan Engine and Hybrid Propulsion System
text:
– Accelerating the Development of Core Propulsion Technologies to Lead the Era of More Electric Aircraft
– Laying the Foundation for Independent Dual-Use Engine Development and Strengthening the Domestic Aviation Propulsion Ecosystem
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced that it held a joint kick-off meeting for the “Next-Generation Dual-Use Aviation Engine and Propulsion System Development Project” on Tuesday, May 26. This milestone marks the official commencement of Korea's first development of a dual-use turbofan engine and hybrid propulsion system, aimed at securing next-generation core technologies in the domestic civil aviation sector.
The joint kick-off meeting was chaired by Changheon Han, Director General of the Aeronautics Innovation Directorate at KASA. It brought together experts from R&D institutions, participating companies, and related entities to conduct in-depth discussions on project implementation strategies and inter-agency cooperation frameworks.
With the overarching goal of securing national strategic technologies in the fields of advanced mobility and aviation, a total budget of approximately 90 billion won will be invested over a four-year period (2026-2029) into the two newly launched projects. The key details are as follows:
1. Development of Core Technologies for High-Bypass Turbofan Engines for Electrified Aircraft
Key Objective: To secure South Korea's first-ever 4,500 lbf-class dual-use aviation gas turbine engine model, adaptable to More Electric Aircraft (MEA) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that require high electrical power output.
Core Tasks: High-bypass ratio fan/booster and combustor testing technologies; design and manufacturing technologies for rotor-integrated Integrated Starter-Generators (ISGs).
2. Advanced Development of Core Technologies for Electric-Turbine Hybrid Propulsion Systems
Key Objective: To develop electric-turbine hybrid propulsion system technologies for next-generation future mobility, alongside their core components: a 500 kW-class turbo generator and a 300 kW-class redundant electric engine (motor/inverter).
Core Tasks: System integrated design, analysis, and ground test rig construction; Development of high-efficiency turbo generators; Development of redundant electric engines (motors and inverters).
Through the “Development of High-Bypass Turbofan Engines for Electrified Aircraft” project, KASA is embarking on a mission to secure the nation's first-ever dual-use aviation engine model (4,500 lbf-class), a milestone that will mark a major turning point in South Korea’s aerospace history. Moving beyond simple component manufacturing, this initiative is expected to serve as a decisive stepping stone for Korea to leap into a global aviation powerhouse by establishing independent engine system integration capabilities.
Alongside engine localization, the “Electric-Turbine Hybrid Propulsion System Development” project, designed to lead the eco-friendly aviation era, was highlighted as a strategic asset that will determine market leadership in future Advanced Air Mobility (AAM). KASA plans to secure the core driving force of the future aviation industry by systematically supporting domestic companies—spanning from core technology development to ground performance validation—thereby enabling them to transform into vital partners within the Global Value Chain (GVC).
Experts attending the kick-off meeting agreed that the localization of aviation engines and propulsion technologies is a paramount task for shifting the domestic aviation industry toward high-value-added structures. They pledged to solidify a collaborative ecosystem to ensure that research outcomes translate into practical business models and strengthened global market competitiveness.
Changheon Han, Director General of the Aeronautics Innovation Directorate at KASA, stated, “High-bypass turbofan engines and hybrid propulsion systems are strategic technologies that will dictate core competitiveness in the next-generation aviation sector.” He added, “We will consolidate domestic capabilities to internalize these critical technologies and leave no stone unturned in project management to ensure we secure a leading edge on the global stage.”

title: KASA Advances Modernization of Korea’s Space Insurance System for the Commercial Launch Era
text:
- First Step Toward Revitalizing the Space Insurance Market Through On-Site Communication in Preparation for the Private-Led Space Economy
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) visited the Korea Defense Guarantee Cooperative in Jung-gu, Seoul, on Tuesday, May 26, and held the 6th Aerospace SOS* Consultation Meeting with representatives from the domestic insurance industry, including the cooperative.
* A communication channel launched in February to respond swiftly to difficulties faced by aerospace companies and identify on-site solutions.
KASA Administrator Taeseog Oh has consistently emphasized the importance of commercial launch services in fostering the growth of the space economy, noting the need to actively expand the number of domestic and international commercial satellite launches to more than two per year.
The meeting was organized to hear firsthand perspectives from the insurance industry and explore ways to revitalize Korea’s domestic space insurance market to support stable private satellite launches and the operation of space assets.
Prior to the meeting, KASA officials reviewed the current status of domestic space insurance underwriting. The review found that the limited underwriting capacity of domestic insurers and the heavy reliance on overseas reinsurance markets have increased cost burdens on private space companies and created barriers to entry for innovative startups.
* Due to the high-cost and high-risk nature of the space industry, domestic insurers typically distribute risk by purchasing reinsurance from overseas insurance companies.
Participants also agreed that revitalizing the domestic space insurance market should go hand in hand with efforts to strengthen the stability and global competitiveness of Korea’s private space companies.
Representatives from participating companies agreed that revitalizing the domestic space insurance market would require clear standards and specialized personnel capable of accurately assessing risks and calculating insurance premiums. They also emphasized that sufficient market demand must first be established to enable the development of viable insurance products.
The participants proposed several policy measures, including: improving legal frameworks related to space insurance coverage and liability limits; developing standard policy terms and operational guidelines for space insurance; developing a pool of specialized professionals and providing technical advisory support; and offering government support to help establish the initial market.
Administrator Taeseog Oh emphasized that “space insurance, which provides risk coverage for private space activities, is an essential infrastructure for the sustainable growth of the space economy.”
He added, “KASA will actively listen to the difficulties faced by the domestic insurance industry and review a range of support measures so that Korean space companies can innovate with confidence, while enabling the domestic space insurance market to grow alongside the broader space economy.”

title: KASA Holds Proclamation Ceremony for the 2nd Aerospace Week
text:
- Aerospace Week to Kick Off on May 23 at the National Science Museum in Daejeon
- Global Aerospace Talent Development Conference Scheduled for May 23 at the Daejeon Convention Center
- 68 Programs Across 12 Metropolitan Cities and Provinces Nationwide; Pilot Opening of the Naro Space Center
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) will hold the Aerospace Week Declaration Ceremony on Saturday, May 23, at the National Science Museum in Daejeon. The event will officially launch Aerospace Week, which will take place for one week from May 23 to 29 ahead of Aerospace Day (May 27).
The ceremony will begin with a pre-event performance by the Daejeon Citizen Observatory Children’s Choir, followed by the official declaration of Aerospace Week. The event will also feature the launch ceremony for the Space Camp, now in its third year, as well as a drone ball performance.
Under the slogan, “Our Technology, Our Space: A New Era of K-Space,” the declaration ceremony will include a celebratory theatrical performance and 18 interactive experience booths. In addition, more than 60 aerospace-themed cultural programs will be held across 12 metropolitan cities and provinces nationwide, providing opportunities for public participation.
The experience booths will feature a variety of engaging and educational content, including exhibitions of actual CubeSats, CanSats, and award-winning entries from robot aircraft competitions; a space exploration VR experience operated by the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI); and hands-on activities organized by university student supporters specializing in aerospace. The event will also include a participatory program titled My Wish to the Moon, where attendees can share their hopes and aspirations for space exploration.
To commemorate Aerospace Week, the Naro Space Center in Goheung-gun, Jeollanam-do, will be opened to the public on a pilot basis. Visitors will have a rare opportunity to tour launch vehicle research facilities, which are normally restricted, through guided bus tours.
Later that afternoon, the Global Aerospace Talent Development Conference will be held at the Daejeon Convention Center.
At the conference, Dr. Holly Miller, the Federal Liaison for the Office of STEM Engagement at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), and Dr. Makoto Natsuisaka of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) will join KASA in presenting their respective countries’ aerospace talent development policies and visions.
In addition, Hyunjoon Kwon, Director General for Aerospace Policy at KASA, will moderate a panel discussion featuring Jaehung Han, Head of the KAIST Space Research Institute; Dr. Insang Moon of the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI); and Changhan Lee of Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI). The panelists will engage in in-depth discussions on cooperation among industry, academia, and research institutions.
KASA Administrator Taeseog Oh stated, “This year’s Aerospace Week has been designed to allow the public to experience aerospace technologies more closely through a variety of programs,” adding, “We ask for the continued interest and support of our people as the Republic of Korea advances toward becoming a global aerospace powerhouse.”

title: CAS500-4 Fully Prepared for Transport to Launch Site
text:
- KASA, the Rural Development Administration, the Korea Forest Service, and KAI Hold Pre-Shipment Review (PSR) Meeting
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh), together with the Rural Development Administration (RDA, Administrator Seungdon Lee) and the Korea Forest Service (KFS, Minister Eunsik Park), announced that they held a Pre-Shipment Review (PSR) for the Compact Advanced Satellite 500-4 (CAS500-4) at the headquarters of Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) on Thursday, May 21, ahead of the satellite’s transportation to the overseas launch site.
The meeting was convened to conduct a final review of the satellite’s technical readiness and transportation safety before transitioning to the launch site shipment phase, following the completion of satellite development and various performance and environmental tests.
Representatives from the RDA and the KFS, the primary user agencies of CAS500-4, as well as KAI, the system integrator, and the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI), the payload developer, participated in the meeting. The participants focused on reviewing satellite development and test results, readiness for satellite imagery mission operations, transportation safety measures, launch schedule and risk management plans.
CAS500-4 is scheduled to begin transportation in June this year and is expected to be launched in July from Vandenberg Space Force Base in the United States. Once operational, the satellite will support wide-area agricultural and forest observation, including crop and forest monitoring activities for the RDA and the KFS.
Hyesun Bang, Director General for Research Policy at the RDA, stated, “We plan to enhance agricultural observation capabilities by advancing satellite-based monitoring of crops and farmland, as well as agricultural disaster risk management systems.”
Jongsu Lee, Director General for Planning and Coordination at the KFS, stated, “We expect the satellite to strengthen our capability to respond to forest disasters through rapid and accurate forest observation, while also enabling early detection of forest changes caused by the climate crisis.”
Jinhee Kim, Director General of the Satellite Division at KASA, emphasized, “CAS500-4 is expected to serve as an important foundation for expanding the utilization of satellite information in the agricultural and forestry sectors. We will continue thorough preparations until the very end to ensure a successful launch and stable mission operations.”

title: KASA Hosts Industry Roundtable to Foster New Ecosystem for Lunar Exploration
text:
- Discussing Private Sector Entry into Lunar Orbit Communication and Navigation Services and Technology Verification Plans
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held a Lunar Orbit Communication Satellite Industry Roundtable at its headquarters in Sacheon on Wednesday, May 20. The meeting aimed to support Korean companies in entering the global lunar exploration market.
The roundtable was organized to gather insights from local enterprises and discuss strategy frameworks for penetrating the global market. Discussions centered on verifying Earth-Moon communication and navigation systems,Oa critical foundation for sustainable lunar exploration and the establishment of lunar economic bases.
Seven leading domestic companies* with expertise in satellite and communication technologies, including space optical communications and lunar infrastructure development, participated in the event.
*Leo Space, SpaceBeam, APSI, LIG D&A, InterGravity Technologies, Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI), and Hanwha Systems.
During the meeting , KASA shared its upcoming mission plans and strategic direction for lunar orbit communication:
ㆍPrivate-sector-led development strategies, 
ㆍSupport mechanisms for establishing global business models, and
ㆍInfrastructure requirements to enable technology demonstration
Participating companies provided valuable feedback on issues such as budget burdens associated with R&D in the capital-intensive space industry, opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises to participate, provision of government-led deep-space exploration infrastructure such as optical communication ground stations, long-term plans for domestic core technology development, and efficient utilization of key personnel.
Kyungin Kang, Director General of the Space Science and Exploration Directorate at KASA, stated, “To ensure domestic companies are competitive in the lunar exploration market, including communication and navigation services, private-sector-led initiatives and technology demonstration opportunities are essential. We will actively support our companies to become key players in the global lunar communication supply chain.”

title: KASA Hosts 5th Aerospace SOS Consultative Meeting on Space Transportation
text:
- Discussions on Revitalizing the Nuri Industry Ecosystem and Developing a Private-Sector-Led Space Transportation Sector
- Emphasizing Stable Launch Opportunities and Public-Private Collaboration
[Relevant National Task] 28-2. Challenging K-Space with Our Own Technology
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held the 5th
Aerospace SOS Consultation Meeting on Thursday, May 14, at Hanwha Aerospace’s 1st Plant in Seongsan-gu, Changwon, Gyeongsangnam-do. The meeting brought together representatives from the industry* to explore ways to revitalize the Nuri rocket (KSLV-II) launch ecosystem and promote private- sector-led growth in the space transportation sector.
*Participating companies (11): Hanwha Aerospace, Korean Aerospace Industry (KAI), Doowon Heavy Industries, Vitzro Nextech, SPACEPRO, S&K Aerospace, Uconsystem, HyLok Corporation, Danam Systems, HIZE Composite Industries and HANYANG ENG.
The meeting provided a platform to hear firsthand industry feedback on the Nuri (KSLV-II) program and discuss practical measures to strengthen competitiveness through sustained Nuri launches.
Hanwha Aerospace, the system integrator, shared the status of preparations for the Nuri’s 5th launch and upcoming missions, highlighting the importance of expanding industry roles and collaboration as launch services transition to private-led operations.
Currently, the assembly of the Nuri 5 vehicle is 70-90% complete, with a targeted launch in the third quarter of 2026. This mission is planned to deploy five microsatellite constellations and ten secondary payload satellites into sun-synchronous orbit.
Participating companies unanimously emphasized that securing stable launch opportunities is a critical factor for revitalizing the launch vehicle industry. They called for continued demand creation and strengthened public-private cooperation to establish a competitive commercial launch service framework.
Administrator Taeseog oh stated, “We will revitalize the space industry ecosystem by building trust and enhancing competitiveness through the continued launch success of Nuri, the backbone of South Korea's space transportation infrastructure." He added, "The government will provide steadfast support so that the private sector can fully unleash its potential by listening closely to industry feedback and establishing effective policies. We also call on enterprises to make proactive investments for the subsequent launches of Nuri."

title: KASA Develops Satellite Imagery AI Training Data Tailored to Industry Needs
text:
- Satellite Imagery AI Datasets Incorporating Industry Feedback to be Released this Year
The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced that it will host the Industry Roundtable on Utilization of Satellite Imagery Big Data and AI Training Data on Friday, May 15, at the Daejeon Convention Center (DCC).
The event aims to identify industry demand for satellite imagery AI training data and explore necessary policy support measures for domestic companies specializing in satellite imagery and artificial intelligence (AI).
The roundtable will bring together companies utilizing satellite imagery AI datasets. KASA and the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) will share the current status of publicly available satellite imagery AI training data and gather feedback from industry on usage needs, challenges, and policy support requirements.
Insights collected during the roundtable will be reflected in the production and distribution methods of satellite imagery AI datasets. Based on this feedback, KASA plans to release the datasets later this year to support technological development within the private sector.
KASA and KARI have continuously released satellite imagery AI training datasets that can be applied across various AI technology development fields.
In 2023 and 2024, a total of 630,000 datasets were released, covering key satellite imagery applications such as object detection, building segmentation, road extraction, cloud detection, and land cover classification. More recently, in 2025 and early this year, an additional 300,000 datasets were released, expanding the applications to include ocean and glacier monitoring, as well as time-series land cover change detection.
These publicly available satellite imagery AI datasets can be conveniently accessed via the national research data platform: DataOn (https://dataon.kisti.re.kr)
The publicly released satellite imagery AI training datasets are being actively utilized by both industry and academia.
SPAID Inc. has applied these datasets to develop 3D geospatial AI solutions, achieving improvements in object detection accuracy, 2D vector extraction, and 3D terrain information precision. Research teams at Seoul National University of Science and Technology have incorporated the datasets into the development of detection models for target objects such as ships and aircraft, as well as educational programs, contributing to the cultivation of talent skilled in satellite imagery applications
Regarding this initiative, Kyungwon Rho, Vice Administrator of KASA, stated, "Moving forward, we will actively promote open access to data from the Korea Multi-Purpose Satellites (KOMPSATs) and the next-generation mid-sized satellites (CAS500s). We will also integrate industry needs and field feedback collected during this roundtable into our policies to strengthen the competitiveness of South Korea’s satellite information industry."
